title: Denaturing RNA Electrophoresis in Urea Polyacrylamide Gels and Semi-Dry Northern Blot Transfer
author: Alice Pawlowski
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beemjbc6
materials: assemble the gel sandwich stack (see pdf in materials section); align plate bottoms with the spacers on a flat surface before sliding the sandwich in the casting clamp assembly and tithening the screws (finger tight to prevent breaking of the plates) place the sandwich into the caster, notched alumina plate facing to the back block; check that black silicone rubber gasket is clean two gels can be prepared in the caster; I suggest always to prepare two (in case that one sandwich is leaky); polymerized gel sandwiches can be stored for later use (see below) prepare the gel according to the table below; 10% PAA is fine to separate fragments of 50 - 200 nt wear Vinyl gloves and goggles! weight 5 g urea and transfer to a 15 ml falcon tube add 2 ml 40% PAA and 1 ml 10 x TBE add a. dest. to a final volume of 10 ml heat at 37 °C with agitation until urea is completely solved (shake occasionaly by hand); this will take a while, you can use higher temperatures (e.g. 55 °C) to speed up the process let the solution cool down add 12 µl TEMED and mix by inverting the tube add 80 µl APS and mix by inverting the tube pour the gel quickly but carefully between the plates using a plastic pasteur pipette remove air bubbles by shortly lifting and pushing the caster to the table insert the comb immediately wait until gel gets solid (at least 1h) remove the gel from the caster and rinse the sandwich with destilled water to remove buffer and gel remnants thoroughly wash caster components in mild detergent and rinse with destilled water immediately after use proceed to step 2 or store the sandwich - wrapped in wet towel paper and foil - for later use at 4-8°C

steps.title: Prepare and denature RNA samples
steps.instruction: Wear gloves, thaw total RNA and the RiboRuler Low Range RNA Ladder on ice, then denature.

substeps.instruction: Mix 5 µl total RNA (≈5 µg; dilute with RNase‑free water if needed) with 5 µl 2× loading dye; incubate 5 min at 95 °C.
Prepare marker: mix 3 µl LR‑ladder, 2 µl RNase‑free water and 5 µl 2× loading dye; incubate 10 min at 70 °C, then snap‑cool on ice.

steps.title: Assemble gel apparatus and load samples
steps.instruction: Set up the urea‑PAGE system, rinse wells, load denatured samples and marker, and connect the power supply.

substeps.instruction: Insert the upper buffer chamber into the lower chamber, clamp the sandwich, and optionally attach a well‑locating decal to the glass plate.
Remove the comb, add 1× TBE buffer to the electrode chambers, and rinse each well thoroughly with a syringe; rinse again immediately before loading.
Quickly spin down the samples in a microcentrifuge, then pipette each sample (and marker) into the appropriate wells.
Close the safety lid and plug the electrodes into the power supply.

steps.title: Run denaturing PAGE
steps.instruction: Electrophorese the gel using a two‑stage current program until the bromophenol blue front exits.

substeps.instruction: Run at constant 10 mA for the first one‑third of the gel length.
Increase to 20 mA for the remainder of the run.
Stop when bromophenol blue (migrates at ~12 nt in 10 % urea‑PAGE) has just run out of the gel.

steps.title: Disassemble gel and stain with EtBr
steps.instruction: Remove the gel, stain with ethidium bromide, image, and return to buffer.

substeps.instruction: Remove the lid, pour off the running buffer, and remove the clamps.
Lift the glass plate using a spacer as a lever; use the spacer to cut off the wells and the upper‑right corner (orientation mark).
Transfer the gel to a clean tray, briefly rinse in 0.5× TBE.
Incubate the gel 15 min in 25 ml 0.5× TBE containing 1 µg/ml ethidium bromide, with gentle agitation in the dark (cover tray with aluminium foil).
While staining, wash the electrophoresis equipment with detergent followed by distilled water; collect the staining solution for reuse.
Rinse the gel once more in 0.5× TBE.
Visualize RNA on a Bio‑Rad Gel‑Doc transilluminator (image area 13.4 × 10.0 cm, nucleic‑acid‑ethidium bromide program) and save the gel picture.
Return the gel to 0.5× TBE buffer.

steps.title: Prepare semi‑dry transfer sandwich
steps.instruction: Cut and soak membrane and filter papers, humidify plates, and assemble the blotting sandwich.

substeps.instruction: Cut one piece of Hybond N+ nylon membrane and eight pieces of 3 MM Whatman paper to the size of the gel; soak all in 0.5× TBE buffer.
Humidify both electrode plates of the Trans‑Blot SD semi‑dry transfer cell with 0.5× TBE.
Assemble the sandwich (bottom up): 4 layers of 3 MM paper, nylon membrane, the PAA gel (remove bubbles with a serological pipette), then 4 more layers of 3 MM paper.

steps.title: Perform electrophoretic transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer RNA from the gel to the nylon membrane using a constant‑current program.

substeps.instruction: Close the transfer cell lid and plug the electrodes.
Run at constant 2 mA · cm⁻² for 45 min (≈180 mA for a 10.0 × 9.0 cm mini‑gel).
Multiple sandwiches may be transferred simultaneously.

steps.title: Process transferred membrane
steps.instruction: Trim, verify, image, UV‑crosslink, dry, and store the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Remove the Whatman paper and cut the membrane with scissors to match the gel size, including the upper‑right corner cut‑off.
Optional: place the gel in 0.5× TBE and check transfer on the transilluminator; successful transfer shows fluorescence only in the uppermost (high‑MW) region.
Transfer the membrane onto a towel sheet, handling only the edges with forceps; place RNA‑side down on the transilluminator table.
Capture a UV image (~0.1 s exposure, nucleic‑acid‑ethidium bromide program, image area 10.0 × 13.4 cm).
Cross‑link RNA to the membrane by UV exposure for 120 s.
Dry the membrane completely, mark the blot with a pencil, and store it between sheets of Whatman paper (or proceed to hybridization).
